title: [Perf][PCP] Fuse direct-KV publication fence
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #52863.

- Fuse peer publication and waiting into one Triton kernel.
- Move epoch advancement from the host onto the device.
- Reduce each direct-KV fence from two kernel launches to one.
- Make epoch advancement work correctly during CUDA graph replay.

## Motivation

#52863 launches separate publish and wait kernels for every direct-KV fence.
These fences execute once per sparse layer, making repeated launch overhead
material in PCP profiles.

Keeping the epoch on the host also prevents a captured CUDA graph from
advancing it on each replay.

title: Use high-priority CUDA stream for overlap scheduling to reduce CPU bubbles
body:
## Motivation

In SGLang's overlap scheduling mode, the scheduler and forward pass run on separate CUDA streams concurrently. The scheduler stream handles request selection and batch preparation while the forward stream runs model inference.

We observed that when the scheduling logic runs on the **default stream**, the CUDA runtime can delay its kernel launches — especially when many streams are active. This creates **CPU bubbles**: idle gaps where the forward stream has finished but the next batch isn't ready because the scheduler hasn't dispatched its kernels in time.

## Changes

1. **Create a dedicated high-priority scheduling stream** (`priority=0`, the highest CUDA stream priority) so that scheduling kernels are dispatched more eagerly by the CUDA runtime, tightening the overlap pipeline.

## Purpose

On CUDA, every tensor-parallel rank runs the sparse-attention (DSA) indexer on every decode row: paged MQA logits, DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate selection or mask, and top-k. Every rank ends up with the same indices. At long context this is a large part of the decode step.

This PR adds an opt-in, `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1`, that splits the decode rows across TP ranks:

- **Metadata builder:** gathers each rank's rows, block-table rows and context lengths into persistent buffers and builds that rank's DeepGEMM schedule. The plan depends only on the padded row count, so CUDA graphs replay with the same buffers.

## Background

`apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch` is the sampler filter used on the small-batch (`batch_size < 8`) GPU path and on CPU. Whenever top-p is requested it sorts the **entire** vocabulary (`logits.sort` over `[B, V]`, e.g. `V=151936` for Qwen3), which dominates the op's cost.

Resolve top-k/top-p from a fixed **top-N candidate window** (`N = 1024`, grown to `k.max()` when a larger top-k is requested) via `torch.topk` instead of a full sort:

body:
The Triton W4A16 GEMM kernel (triton_w4a16_gemm_kernel) loads quantization
scales and zero points from a single group index per BLOCK_K tile, but the
kernel launcher does not enforce BLOCK_K <= group_size. When BLOCK_K

title: Fix inflated row pitch when a CP round-robin shard has a single row
body:
## Motivation

`dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data` can hand downstream kernels a shard whose row pitch is `cp_size` times too large, which on DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism causes a GPU memory fault.

The last line of the function is

```python
return input_.view(-1, cp_size, *input_.shape[1:])[:, cp_rank].contiguous()
```

When a prefill chunk holds exactly `cp_size` tokens, every rank's shard has a **single row**. A size-1 outer dimension imposes no contiguity constraint, so `is_contiguous()` returns `True` regardless of `stride(0)` — and `.contiguous()` becomes a no-op. The shard keeps the `cp_size`-inflated row pitch, `cp_size * row_numel` instead of `row_numel`.

title: fix(triton): define masked softcap loads
body:
## Summary

Fixes #27074.

The softcap Triton kernels load masked vectors without an explicit `other` value. Triton's `tl.load` leaves masked-out lanes undefined when `other` is omitted, so the tail lanes can feed undefined values through the softcap math before the final masked store.

This sets `other=0.0` on the two masked softcap loads in `softcap.py`. The value is neutral for the invalid lanes because those lanes are not stored, and it keeps the intermediate math defined.

## Purpose

`VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1` delegation (#50081) execs `vllm-bench` with the raw argv, so Python-documented flags must parse in the Rust CLI. The speed-bench flags had drifted:

- `--speed-bench-output-len` did not exist in Rust — it failed with `unexpected argument`, and without it the output length silently fell back to `--sharegpt-output-len` → `--random-output-len` (default **128** vs Python's **4096**), making delegated speed-bench results non-comparable. This was also reported by a user on Slack (`vllm bench serve` rejecting `--speed-bench-output-len` while `--help=all` lists it, on a build from the pre-#50081 default-delegation window).
